title: C# Questions & Answers - Bitwise and Conditional Operators
sourceFile: Bitwise & Conditional Operators - C# Multiple Choice Questions - Sanfoundry.html
description: This set of C# Multiple Choice Questions & Answers focuses on "Bitwise and Conditional Operators".

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The bitwise AND (&) operator compares corresponding bits. 10 (1010) AND 20 (10100) results in 0 (00000). 10 (1010) AND 10 (1010) results in 10 (1010).

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The bitwise OR (|) operator returns 1 if either of the bits is 1. 10 (01010) OR 20 (10100) = 11110 (30). 10 OR 10 = 10.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
Which of the following options is NOT a bitwise operator in C#?
questions.explanation: += and -= are compound assignment operators, not bitwise operators.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: In C#, the bitwise OR assignment operator (|=) can be used with boolean types. 'true | false' results in 'true'.

questions.question: Choose the correct code snippet to complete the Main method to calculate 'res' using a conditional operator.

options.text: Both A and B are valid

questions.explanation: In C#, the conditional operator (?:) must be part of an expression. Both A and B assign the result of the ternary expression to 'res'. Option C is invalid because 'return' is a statement, not an expression.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: 1) y > 10 is false. 2) !(false) is true. 3) Since true, 'x = y + 3' (8) is executed. Variable x becomes 8, and y remains 5.

questions.question: Which of the following is the conditional (ternary) operator in C#?
questions.explanation: The ternary operator '?:' is the only conditional operator in C# that takes three operands.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: 1) 4 % 2 is 0, so b is true (prints 'True'). 2) 4 / 2 is 2, so the if condition is true (prints 'true').

questions.question: Arrange these C# operators in order of increasing precedence (lowest to highest).
questions.explanation: The correct order from lowest to highest precedence is: Conditional (?:), Conditional AND (&&), Bitwise AND (&), Equality (!=), and finally Unary (++).
